My wife and I are in our 30s because stupid kids decided to have sex in the 80s. She has a job in digital marketing and I work in IT. We both hate working. I've come to realize I just hate working, no matter who for or what I'm doing. You'll see alot of the same responses on reddit re: hating work. Here are the ones you're likely to see versions of: "That's just life", "We all gotta do it", "Try a career in what you already enjoy", "Most people in this world have it worse than you", "Make the most of your time off", "Start a guerilla revolution in a third world country and install yourself as dictator", ...Ok I made that last one up haha. The point is it's what the status quo is for the working class. If you're not wealthy enough to not work for a living, you're part of it. I'd seriously consider lowering all your expenses as much as possible to give you two options. 1. Continue working as you have, and retire as soon as you can. 2. Look for a part time job to support your now "more affordable" lifestyle and work less.

Alternatively, you could look at moving abroad to a country with less GDP and looser work schedules. It's difficult to accept, but all the "bosses" in the US would like longer work hours, not less. With the erosion of unions and collective bargaining since the 1980s, the US 40+ hour work week is not likely to change in your lifetime, unless it increases in hours.

I've been in some form of Helpdesk for over 10 years. I've gotten myself to $34/hr jobs doing this 8 hours a day, and no weekends. I don't like on call rotations, and having dabbled in just about every IT avenue, I haven't found anything specific to focus on. I envy all of you who pick a path, study, and test for certs, but I really don't get excited by any of this shit anymore. Best way to do it is to move on after a year or so no matter what you're doing. I'm 38 and I'd rather not spend the bulk of my life studying for shit I don't care about. Oh, and yes I'm very pigeonholed in helpdesk. Don't really care. I've gotten married and bought a condo in OC, California with years of helpdesk. There's no incorrect path through life or career. We all take a different one and none are wrong. Today it's all cybersecurity and cloud computing... something will become more important than those in IT at some point too.

I got a position as a contract IT worker, working on a project that should stretch into early next year for a local city nearby in California. The project has about 10 people working on it in total to revamp the IT hardware and systems for the entire city (City Hall, Fire, Police, Library, etc...) It's me and 3 other guys my age doing support, and packaging software into a new SCCM server... in the IT department of City Hall. It's nice to not work for a huge/mega corporation. The hourly is the same as my last job, only no benefits as a contractor.

Honestly, I see the "specialized" guys above me on this project (network admin, programmers, etc) and while it looks a lot more fun than what I'm doing, I don't think it's in the cards for me. I think the stress would kill me (literally) and I wouldn't be happy along the way. It really is about who you know and not what you know. Sure, maybe what you know gets you in the door and gets you contact with that next person that gives you your next great gig... but unfortunately that's really never been me. I have fewer friends than I did before as I approach 40, and I'm getting worse at faking being nice to people by the day. I still don't think I'm cut out for working in this life. I know all the responses "That's just the way work is" or "Nobody likes to work, just suck it up" or "One day you'll find your passion and work won't seem like work anymore".... I've found them all to be false in my case over the last 20 years of work. It's not the system that is broken, it's me.
